sites.rationale: ACKR1/DARC is a 7-TM protein with no signal peptide; the extracellular N-terminus spans residues 1–60 (60 aa) before TM1 begins at residue 61 (A). An N-terminal FLAG prepend (insert_after_residue=0, residue_after=M) places the tag entirely within this 60-aa extracellular domain, ≥60 residues from the TM1 boundary, satisfying all distance and steric constraints. The paper names no specific junction residue, so position_evidence is topology_derived: with only one extracellular terminus on a 7-TM protein, the N-terminal prepend is the only possible location for an N-terminal tag. Python confirmed residue 1 = M and residue 61 = A from the numbered sequence. Full-length DARC/ACKR1 cloned in pcDNA3.1 with an N-terminal FLAG tag for cell-surface expression studies; a second construct in pVL1393 added the M4 receptor N-terminal region (residues 2–23) after the FLAG tag as a trafficking aid. ACKR1 has no signal peptide (UniProt P23945); the N-terminus (residues 1–60) is directly extracellular, making the N-terminal prepend the sole extracellular terminus. The paper names no specific residue junction, but with exactly one extracellular terminus the position is unambiguous.

sources.claim: The cDNA coding region of DARC was cloned in pcDNA3.1 vector with an N-terminal FLAG tag and in pVL1393 vector with an N-terminal FLAG tag followed by the N-terminal region of M4 receptor (residue no. 2-23).

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) was provided. It reports a full-length, membrane-anchored FLAG-tagged DARC/ACKR1 construct used for cell-surface expression studies — this qualifies under the rules (full-length, membrane-anchored, tag tolerated on the surface). No residue number is named in the clip, but ACKR1 has no signal peptide and its N-terminus (residues 1–60) is the sole extracellular terminus, so the position is topology-derived rather than validated. The second construct in L1 (pVL1393 with M4 receptor residues 2–23 appended after the FLAG tag) is a trafficking-enhancement variant of the same N-terminal tag site, not a separate site. No other ledger lines were provided, so no internal loop sites (ECL1 119–130, ECL2 188–207, ECL3 263–283) could be proposed — the ledger does not support them.
